validated_results.title: Animal foods, protein, calcium and prostate cancer risk: the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition.
validated_results.reason: Prospective cohort study investigating dietary calcium intake and incident prostate cancer risk in the EPIC cohort.

sample_size.excerpt: After an average of 8.7 years of follow-up, 2727 men were diagnosed with prostate cancer among the 142 520 participants included in this study, with a total of 1 236 265 person-years.

cases.excerpt: After an average of 8.7 years of follow-up, there were 2727 incident cases of prostate cancer, of which 1131 were known to be localised and 541 advanced-stage disease.

effect_size.excerpt: Protein derived from all animal or all plant foods was not significantly associated with risk. Total dietary calcium intake and calcium intake from dairy foods were also associated with an increased risk (HR for the highest versus the lowest fifth of intake were 1.17, 95% CI: 1.00–1.35; P trend =0.01 for total dietary calcium, and 1.18, 95% CI: 1.03–1.36; P trend =0.02 for dairy calcium).
